lede: The tasks people bring to AI models account for 21 percent of US wages, pay has stayed within its usual range while the mix of jobs has shifted more than in any three years since 2013, and 41 percent of new degrees are in fields that lead to the most exposed jobs.
meaning: The tasks people bring to AI models are paid about a fifth of all the wages in the United States, while pay across the skills behind them has moved no further over the last three years than in an ordinary stretch of the record, so these models already reach a wide share of paid work and there is no sign yet that employers pay for those skills differently.

The reading that stands out is the mix of work: over the last three years employment has moved toward jobs that draw on arts and humanities by more than in any three-year stretch since 2013, although a record of thirteen years produces a shift that size by chance about one time in eleven, and the same test was passed in 2020 and 2021, when the pandemic reshuffled employment, so the next release of the wage tables will show whether it holds.

Degrees are the slow channel and the one policy can count: 40.7 percent of new bachelor's degrees in 2024 went to the most exposed third of fields, against 40.3 percent in 2023, and people who move into those jobs from other occupations will join the count once the flows between occupations are published.

city.how: For each skill group the index takes the last three yearly changes in pay, and in the share of employment, and sets them against that group's own changes since 2013: a change stands out when it passes the level only the most extreme three-year stretches in the record reached, and both the reading and that level are recalculated with each spring release of the wage tables.

valley.how: Degrees come from the IPEDS completions file and each field of study is scored by the exposure of the occupations its graduates hold, on the task measure of Eloundou and coauthors, so the share moves once a year, and people who arrive in exposed jobs from other occupations will join this view when the flows between occupations are published.
